question: In September 2024, the European Court of Auditors published a report on organic farming in the EU. The report flagged gaps relating to quantifiable targets for objectives and actions, as well as a lack of indicators with which to monitor progress. The only objective for the organic sector, namely to have 25% of agricultural land be organically farmed, is non-binding and is intended only to increase the area. 1.
Does the Commission plan to strengthen the performance criteria? If so, how and by when?

The Court points out that five Member States alone accounted for 62% of the EAFRD budget allocated to organic farming between 2014 and 2022. What initiatives has the Commission planned to support the development of organic farming in Europe in light of the differences between Member States?

The Court states that training and advisory services should be provided to farmers to allow them to build necessary knowledge. According to the report, farmers face an administrative and financial burden when they decide to convert to organic farming. Will the Commission take action in relation to this?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (15.11.2024) 1. The Action Plan1 on the 25% target includes other quantitative targets like dedicating at least 30% of the Horizon Europe2 budget for research and innovation actions on agriculture, forestry and rural areas to topics specific to or relevant for the organic sector. Others (on e.g. public procurement, sales) were not retained because premature or not credible.

The actions in the Plan were formulated in a concrete manner enabling easy monitoring. The Commission does not envisage any changes to the current Plan as this is a prerogative of the incoming Commission. 2. The Commission has successfully encouraged Member States to develop comprehensive national strategies on organic production.

Under the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP)3 2023-2027, the planned share of the utilised agricultural area to be supported under the Strategic Plans for organic farming almost doubled (to about 10%) compared to the previous period. Member States with low budgets allocated to organic farming have increased their efforts. National ambitions range from 2.5% to 23.

7 % of the respective utilised agricultural areas to be organically farmed. The Commission will continue to encourage Member States to support organic farming under the CAP and to align support for organic farming more with the needs and challenges identified in the organic sector.

It is logical that the biggest Member States together make up a high share of the total budget for organic farming support, which reflects the size of the agricultural area covered. 3. Efforts to include training and advise on organic farming have been strengthened under the current CAP and several Member States (e.g.
Slovenia, Bulgaria) include a requirement for training in the area-based support for organic farming.
1 Action Plan for the Development of Organic Production (COM(2021) 141). 2 https://research-and-innovation.ec.europa.eu/funding/funding-opportunities/funding-programmes-and-open-
